segments.seen: A first-person view of a person's legs standing on a vast, cracked frozen ocean at sunset with the title 'FROZEN OCEAN: HOW DEEP DO YOU GO?'
segments.heard: Imagine the ocean frozen over. Pick your depth.

segments.seen: A sequence of eight depth scenarios: surface ice, under-ice algae, 10m ice keels, 50m dim water, 200m rock face, 1km basalt arch, abyssal seafloor pillows, and a hydrothermal vent.
segments.heard: One: standing on endless ice, wind howling. Two: right under the ice, faint light leaking through. Three: ten metres down, freezing blue twilight. Four: fifty metres, the last light fades. Five: two hundred metres. Total black. Six: one kilometre. Crushing cold, no light. Seven: the seafloor, kilometres under the ice. Eight: beside a superheated vent.

segments.seen: The under-ice scene from option two returns with text explaining the 20-metre photosynthesis limit, followed by the opening sunset ice scene.
segments.heard: Real answer: number 2, because photosynthesis can work under ice up to 20 metres thick. Life may have found a foothold there. Comment your number.
